short: 38-phoneme intracortical classification (M06) is standard: isolated-phoneme sets preceded it in EMG, one participant, no repetition; bins, not trials, were split into folds.
position: The paper [@brumberg2011classification] changes one component, the decoder (M06): it replaces the same participant's continuous three-vowel formant control [@guenther2009] with classification of 38 attempted phonemes, against prior intracranial classifiers of four phonemes (Blakely et al. 2008, cited by the target) and ten overt words [@kellis2010decoding]; the one prior intracranial decoding design in the ledger has no discrete unit set (Appendix). It is standard, not ahead: isolated phonemes of nearly a full inventory had been classified from subvocal EMG (Jorgensen and Binsted 2005, as described by [@walliczek2006subword]), 40 phone classes were units of continuous recognition from ultrasound and lip video [@hueber2008phone], and nothing repeats the result beyond one participant, as the authors state. The evaluation (M12) is standard for 2011, but bins, not trials, were assigned to folds (inference from the fold counts), the strongest confound for the 16–21% accuracies. Their "truly not great enough to be useful as a communication device" holds; their "lower-bound on the possible classification/prediction performance" is unsupported, because mixing a trial's bins across folds biases accuracy upward (inference).
